title: というより — “rather than ～ / more like …”
summary: Plain form / noun + というより means “rather than saying ～, it is more accurate to say ….” The speaker corrects or refines the first description with a more suitable one. The second half is the speaker's real view.

patterns.form: 名詞／普通形 ＋ というより、〜
patterns.gloss: noun / plain form + というより (優しいというより、料理というより)
A というより B: B is a better description than A

body.p: A is the common or expected description, and B is a better one. 彼は優しいというより、気が弱い. Both A and B are in the same kind of form: adjective with adjective, noun with noun. な-adjectives and nouns drop だ.
A is not denied completely; it is just judged less suitable than B. The speaker is adjusting the description. Often B is a less flattering or more precise word.
The longer ～というよりむしろ ... adds “rather” for emphasis. The sentence-final version AというよりBに近い (closer to B than A) is also common.

examples.ja: 彼（かれ）は優（やさ）しいというより、気（き）が弱（よわ）い。
examples.romaji: Kare wa yasashii to iu yori, ki ga yowai.
examples.tr: Rather than kind, he's just timid.

examples.ja: これは料理（りょうり）というより、芸術（げいじゅつ）作品（さくひん）だ。
examples.romaji: Kore wa ryōri to iu yori, geijutsu sakuhin da.
examples.tr: This is a work of art rather than a dish.

examples.ja: 彼女（かのじょ）は歌手（かしゅ）というより、俳優（はいゆう）に近（ちか）い。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa kashu to iu yori, haiyū ni chikai.
examples.tr: She is closer to an actor than a singer.

pitfalls: Do not use だ before というより: 優しいというより, 歌手というより (not 歌手だというより).
It compares two descriptions of the same thing. Do not use it to compare two different things; use より alone.
